item.title: Kosovo's ex-President Thaci convicted of war crimes, sentenced to 25 years in prison
item.description: A European Union-backed court convicted former Kosovo President Hashim Thaci of war crimes committed during his country's war for independence from Serbia and sentenced him to 25 years in prison.
item.content:encoded:
A European Union-backed court convicted former Kosovo President Hashim Thaci of war crimes committed during his country's war for independence from Serbia and sentenced him to 25 years in prison.

(Image credit: Koen van Weel)
item.dc:creator: The Associated Press

item.title: Saudi Arabia calls an attempted Mecca attack a 'red line' as Houthis deny they did it
item.description: Saudi Arabia accused Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels overnight of trying to attack Islam's holiest city, prompting condemnation from countries in the region but no sign of military support.

item.title: Turkish habit of stashing gold "under the pillow' hurts economy, government says
item.description: For years, Turks have stashed their gold at home against a raining day, mistrustful of banks. Now the government says that tradition hurts the economy

item.title: Turks often keep gold as a hedge against inflation. It may be hurting Turkey's future
item.description: Billions of dollars worth of gold is held in Turkish households outside the banking system. The government aims to convince citizens to put it into the mainstream financial system to help the economy.

item.title: SCOTUS rejects Trump's mail voting limits. And, the Kennedy Center financial crisis
item.description: The Supreme Court has rejected Trump's mail-in voting restrictions ahead of the midterm elections. And, the Kennedy Center says it is on the brink of bankruptcy and could close soon.

item.title: Trump says Ukraine and Russia agreed to stop attacks on energy sites
item.description: In the face of soaring diesel prices, President Trump claims Ukraine and Russia have agreed to halt strikes on each other's energy sites.

item.title: Air pollution spiked after the Trump administration stopped embassy monitoring
item.description: In 2025, the Trump administration ended a long-running program to collect air pollution data at U.S. embassies. A new study suggests that led to a 24-33% increase in local pollution levels.
item.content:encoded:
